scores.evidence: "The decisive choice was made while the race was stopped" — verdict opens each section before evidence
"What the timing data cannot see" functions as a closing disclaimer section, partially wrapping up limitations — not a full synthesis but not clean either
No bridging sentences between sections; headings do all transitional work throughout
"13.7s behind the leader... cost about 31 seconds... difference is roughly 18 seconds" — three figures stacked in one paragraph rather than deployed singly
"that figure is an estimate rather than a measured counterfactual" and "labelled as one" — hedges are explicit and owned without collapsing
Russell is the persistent benchmark for Antonelli throughout; comparison is structural, not incidental
"CAR 12 (ANT) TIME 1:28.582 DELETED - TRACK LIMITS AT TURN 1 LAP 49" inserted as hard stop confirming the gap reversal
"Gasly, from Alpine's first pole, was second by lap 2, sixth by lap 10" — positional sequence narrated rather than interpreted in the midfield section
"Nobody could see it yet, but that was the race" — flat, dry, juxtaposition-based; no exclamation or flourish
"I think this is the part the 19th-to-first line hides" — first person flags a judgment call, appears once, not decoratively
Names and jargon (VSC, green-flag stop, lane time) used without definition or introduction throughout
Lap-28 paragraph runs five sentences making three distinct points (stop, Verstappen, cost estimate) — exceeds one-point-per-paragraph rule
"The medium car was quicker on equal-age rubber and still could not pass. I think this is the part the 19th-to-first line hides" — long analytical then short punchy throughout
The VSC stop and tyre strategy sections get the most room; the midfield rest-of-grid section gets two compressed sentences per driver

top_fixes: E1: The lap-28 paragraph stacks 13.7s, 31s, and 18s into a single unit — split across sentences or paragraphs so each figure lands alone as its own clinching moment rather than a cascade of arithmetic.

R1/S2: The 'rest of the grid' and 'timing data cannot see' sections drift toward narration and limitation-listing respectively; the midfield section should interpret Gasly's collapse and Pérez's penalty rather than sequence them, and the final section reads like a methods disclosure — cut or compress to a single dry aside.

P1: The VSC stop paragraph is doing five things at once; separate Verstappen's parallel stop into its own short paragraph to restore the one-point-per-paragraph discipline and sharpen the contrast between the two drivers' decisions.
